text:
Gita (Head of Eng Ops): Dropping a quick follow-up from today's all-hands about release cadence, oncall handoffs, quality gates and SLAs. Putting a short thread so teams can comment.

Arjun (VP Eng): TL;DR: aim for a predictable cadence. Major releases = 3-week cycle. Minor/patches = weekly windows. Hotfixes go through a fast-track with ops sign-off.

Marco (Eng Manager): Can we have a tiny checklist for "ready to cut"? CI green, perf sanity, doc blurb, rollout plan?

Tess (SRE): +1 checklist. Also add: traffic ramp plan and at least one rollback point. For oncall: pilot 2w primary + 1w overlap (shadow) to reduce burnout.

Arjun (VP Eng): Pilot sounds good for runtime and api teams. If noise increases revert.

Gita (Head of Eng Ops): About quality bars: propose blocking if golden-set evals show >4% relevance drop OR >5% hallucination increase OR 95p latency regresses >10%. Open to tuning per model family.

Marco (Eng Manager): If a release is blocked, what's the escalation? Who signs off after mitigation?

Tess (SRE): Protocol: model owner ack within 4 business hours, mitigation plan within 24h. If unresolved, release lead + product + reliability make the call within 48h. We'll add flowchart to the runbook.

lighthouse-bot: Reminder: new oncall overlap template published: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/oncall-overlap (auto)

Gita (Head of Eng Ops): Action items: @Tess to PR oncall pilot schedule + handoff template by EOW; @Marco to draft minimal release checklist; @Arjun to share hotfix fast-track steps. Please drop edge cases here (cross-service migrations, infra-only rollouts).

Arjun (VP Eng): Thanks everyone. Short and actionable. I'll follow up with a 1-page summary after we collect PRs. :thumbsup:
